page: Amazon Web Services m7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing and LLM inference speed for text generation using a small 135M model also demonstrate strong to top-tier results, with the latter reaching the top 10% tier at 338.71 tokens per second. Conversely, multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU tests, fall into the average category. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes, along with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, consistently register within the middle 50% of tested servers.

A notable hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached options, which may impact I/O-intensive tasks. The server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory deliver solid resource density for general-purpose workloads. This hardware profile is suitable for applications requiring strong single-thread execution, such as text processing, software compilation, web serving, and small-scale language model inference, while serving as a balanced node for general-purpose enterprise applications.
